Introduction to SATOM

What SATOM is, which Fortinet appliances it manages, and the working principles behind every page of the console.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator

What is SATOM?#

SATOM (System Automation & Task Orchestration Manager) is a multi-user web console for operating a fleet of Fortinet application-delivery and analytics appliances from one place. Instead of signing in to every appliance and clicking through its own GUI, you register the appliances once and then browse, change, back up, upgrade and monitor them from SATOM.

It covers five product families, each in its own workspace (called an ADOM, see ADOMs and products):

Product What SATOM does with it
FortiWeb (web application firewall) Server policies, server objects, web protection profiles, exceptions and signatures, backups, firmware, configuration sections.
FortiADC (application delivery controller) The appliance's own menu (load balancing, WAF, network, …), signatures and an API console.
FortiAuthenticator (identity and access) Users, groups, tokens, certificates and RADIUS/TACACS+ clients read from the unit, plus an API console.
FortiAnalyzer (logging and analytics) Device manager, log and report views and a JSON-RPC API console.
FortiGate (next-generation firewall) The device's own GUI pages read live, with cmdb edits (dry run first, read back and verified), an API console whose writes are dry-run by default, and the FortiOS menu's sections — interfaces, firewall policies, objects, security profiles, VPN, users, system — as read-only pages. See FortiGate.

On top of the five product workspaces there is a Global workspace: one console spanning the whole fleet (dashboard, monitoring, search, jobs, certificates and administration). See Global home.

ℹ️Note

SATOM is not a FortiManager or a firewall-policy tool. It manages application-delivery, identity and analytics appliances; its FortiGate workspace edits one cmdb object at a time on one FortiGate, with no fleet rollouts, backups or firmware. The product name and the "About" card on your profile page always show the running version.

Who it is for#

Audience Typical use
Viewer Look at policies, health, metrics and backups without changing anything.
Operator Day-to-day changes: policies, objects, exceptions, backups, upgrades inside an approved window.
Administrator Users and profiles, settings, appliance registration, automations, the database and SATOM's own updates.
Advanced user Engineers using the API, the Python console, Report Studio or Lua Studio.

What each person can do is decided by their profile (a set of granular permissions). The three profiles shipped with SATOM are readonly, operator and admin; administrators can compose others. See Users and profiles and Permissions.

How SATOM works — the principles you will notice everywhere#

It reads from its own copy first#

SATOM keeps a local, queryable copy of every appliance's configuration (filled by Rediscovery and Deep capture). Most pages render from that copy, so they stay fast and usable even when an appliance is slow, unreachable or licence-locked. Pages that do this show how fresh the data is; when you need the current state of the box, use the page's refresh-from-device control.

Changes are previewed before they are applied#

Writes to an appliance are prepared first and shown as a preview of what will be sent. Nothing reaches the appliance until you confirm. Applied changes are recorded in the Audit Log with before/after history.

Long work runs as a job#

Backups, discoveries, bulk changes and firmware work run as background jobs. You can keep navigating while they run; a dock tracks their progress and the notifications bell tells you when they finish.

Risky work goes through change control#

A firmware upgrade is bound to an approved change request and runs inside its maintenance window. Recurring housekeeping runs as scheduled actions.

Every workspace is scoped#

Each ADOM only shows its own product's appliances, jobs, notifications and bookmarks. The Global ADOM shows everything. The ADOM is remembered per browser tab, so you can keep FortiWeb open in one tab and FortiADC in another.

Getting help inside the console#

  • Documentation — the link on the sign-in page opens this documentation. Since 3.1.0 the sidebar no longer links it.
  • Concept Map — the link in the page footer lists every page grouped by what it is for. See Concept Map.
  • Report a problem — in the Tools menu (wrench icon in the top bar). It sends a short report to the administrators together with the page you were on. See Navigation.
